{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "resolution_efficiency",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "incident_category",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "A clean, human-readable categorical (printer, monitor, network, etc.) with well-separated, well-populated categories. Segmenting resolution efficiency by concrete incident category is directly informative and refines the coarse original 'category' field."
    },
    {
      "name": "resolution_action_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable categories (repair, investigation, update_install, configuration, replacement) that plausibly relate to how long/efficiently incidents are resolved. Good separation and populated buckets make it a strong exploratory segmentation."
    },
    {
      "name": "failure_symptom",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Meaningful, interpretable symptom categories (not_responding, display_issue, paper_jam, etc.). Some tail categories are tiny (service_failed_to_start=1) but the main buckets are populated enough to compare efficiency across symptoms."
    },
    {
      "name": "reassignment_occurred",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "A crisp binary with a healthy split (303/193). Reassignment is a classic, highly interpretable process variable expected to correlate with resolution efficiency, enabling clear grouped comparison."
    },
    {
      "name": "caller_type",
      "role": "irrelevant",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "Despite its name suggesting a type, the values are individual person names (David_Loo, Don_Goodliffe) mixed with a role (ITIL_user). This is a mislabelled identifier-like field, not a coherent 'type' segmentation, and offers little interpretable relationship to efficiency."
    },
    {
      "name": "software_trigger",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Binary flag with a usable split (440/60). Whether an incident was software-triggered is interpretable and can be compared against efficiency, though the minority class is somewhat small."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 5,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.72,
  "rationale": "As a set, the added columns strongly support interpretable, well-separated segmentations of resolution efficiency: incident_category, resolution_action_type, failure_symptom, reassignment_occurred, and software_trigger are all external, associational variables with human-readable categories or clean binaries. They meaningfully extend the requested category/priority/assignment_group breakdown. The main weakness is caller_type, which is effectively a person-identifier rather than a genuine 'type' and adds little groupable signal, and a couple of columns have very small minority/tail categories. Overall the set realises the exploratory-relationship claim well."
}
